final_rationale: The Actor narrowed the position in a policy-bounded way and conceded several weaknesses, but that is a reinterpretation of the same admissible record, not new admissible evidence. The existing evidence supports aggregate launch readiness, the existence of an unresolved cybersecurity alert-triage weakness, and the insufficiency of the draft runbook as a caveat-removing mitigation. It does not support caveat-free certification, and it also does not establish the actual disclosure or approval state required to move to compliant_with_caveats. The key distinction is that a caveated certification theory may be conceptually more defensible than clean certification, but compliance still depends on evidence that the caveat/disclosure condition has actually been satisfied or otherwise approved. That evidence is absent here, so the initial concern set remains open.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still does not show that the required disclosure was actually made in the model card; the Actor concedes this gap.
The current model-card draft still says there are no known material limitations, which remains in tension with the proposed certification basis.
The mitigation runbook is still draft and still lacks a defined owner and alert threshold, so it cannot satisfy the policy standard for removing caveats.
There is still no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is still no standalone admissible materiality determination tying the cybersecurity alert-triage weakness to a named launch use case, even though the policy turns on that predicate.
